suppress.notes: False positive on spring-security 7.1.0. CVE-2026-47838 (X.509 SubjectDnX509PrincipalExtractor username confusion) only affects the 5.7.x-6.5.x lines; the equivalent 7.x issue was tracked as CVE-2026-22747 and fixed in 7.0.5. Matched via the broad vendor-level pivotal_software/vmware spring_security CPEs, which lack version-line granularity. See https://spring.io/security/cve-2026-47838/

Not exploitable through this library. CVE-2026-59889 (@JsonView bypass for @JsonUnwrapped properties during deserialization) genuinely affects jackson-databind 3.0.0-3.1.4, but the vulnerable path requires combining @JsonView-based write authorization with @JsonUnwrapped and readerWithView(). This starter only deserializes a flat {username, password} login body and uses neither annotation. Fixed upstream in 3.1.5; remove this suppression once Spring Boot manages jackson-databind >= 3.1.5. See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5gvw-p9qm-jgwh

Not exploitable through this library. CVE-2026-13006 (arbitrary code execution via Janino-evaluated <if condition> in logback configuration) affects logback-core up to 1.5.36, but exploitation requires the Janino library on the classpath (absent by default, not a dependency of this starter) plus an attacker with write access to the logback configuration and high local privileges (CVSS vector AV:L/PR:H) - i.e. an attacker who already has code-execution-equivalent access. Definitively fixed upstream in 1.5.37 (Janino-based conditionals removed); remove this suppression once Spring Boot manages logback >= 1.5.37. See https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-13006 and https://logback.qos.ch/news.html

Not exploitable through this library. CVE-2026-49844 (malformed JSON emitted by MapMessage.asJson() for non-finite floats) does live in the log4j-api jar, but this starter only carries log4j-api as the SLF4J bridge facade routing to Logback: log4j-core and JsonTemplateLayout are not on the classpath and the log4j-to-slf4j bridge formats via getFormattedMessage(), never asJson(). Impact even if reachable is limited to log integrity (malformed JSON), not RCE or DoS. Fixed upstream in 2.25.5; remove this suppression once Spring Boot manages log4j >= 2.25.5. See https://logging.apache.org/security.html

Not exploitable in embedded Tomcat as configured by Spring Boot. These CVEs genuinely affect Tomcat 11.0.22 but every one of them requires a feature that a default Spring Boot REST application (the only supported deployment of this starter) never activates: - CVE-2026-59083, CVE-2026-53404: RewriteValve rewrite rules used as a security boundary (no RewriteValve is configured by Spring Boot). - CVE-2026-55955, CVE-2026-59084: Tribes clustering EncryptInterceptor (clustering is never enabled for embedded Tomcat; 59084 is additionally a documentation-only fix). - CVE-2026-53434: FFM/OpenSSL connector with CRL-based client-cert revocation (Spring Boot uses the NIO connector; no mTLS/CRL configuration). - CVE-2026-55956, CVE-2026-55276: container-managed security constraints in web.xml (authorization is handled by Spring Security filters, not Tomcat security constraints; 55276 is a logging-fidelity defect behind logEffectiveWebXml only). - CVE-2026-50229: XSS in the "number guess" examples webapp of the full Tomcat distribution, which is not part of the tomcat-embed-core jar at all. All are fixed in Tomcat 11.0.23/11.0.24; remove this suppression once Spring Boot manages tomcat >= 11.0.24. See https://tomcat.apache.org/security-11.html
